aboutH2: Peak House: Youth Addiction Treatment in Vancouver, British Columbia
intro: Peak House is a residential treatment facility that provides a 10-week live-in program for adolescents aged 13 to 18 who want to overcome their addiction to drugs or alcohol. The program is voluntarily entered into by residents who have made a conscious decision to seek help. Pacific Youth and Family Services Society runs the program with support from the Vancouver Coastal Health Authority. Being Carf accredited and licensed, Peak House is seen as a reputable choice for families seeking rehabilitation for their loved ones.

pillars.title: Home-like Campus
pillars.body: The cheerful campus of Peak House is in a residential area of Vancouver, British Columbia, reminding the residents that they are part of a larger community. The facility features a big backyard, a full kitchen, a living room, seven bedrooms with eight beds, and two group rooms, with a decor that is warm and welcoming. The ambiance of the house fosters a sense of safety that residents find comforting. Being an LGBT+ affirming facility, it is inclusive where diversity is celebrated.

pillars.title: Therapeutic Activities
pillars.body: The program at Peak House strikes a balance between therapeutic work and fun activities that help the residents rediscover activities that can be enjoyed without using drugs or alcohol. Residents receive individual and group counseling, participate in education programs, engage in physical activities, use holistic health techniques, and even get to listen to guest speakers. Arts and music are also part of the curriculum, as are regular outings to the community. Former residents have commended the approach, saying that it helps create the necessary mindset for success.

pillars.title: Aftercare and Going Back to School
pillars.body: The last three weeks at Peak House go into aftercare planning, ideally with family and the young person's own counsellor involved, so the move home is worked out before it happens. Once youth leave, they are encouraged to come back for four aftercare therapy sessions, alone or with family, and staff are available by phone. A staff-led group meets monthly for former residents, and some come back to talk with current residents about staying substance free. The Vancouver School Board teacher can also send an education report to the home school, which gives teachers there something to build the next learning plan on.

overview: Peak House is a leading rehab center that specializes in youth treatment for those facing substance misuse challenges. The center offers a ten-week voluntary program that provides a live-in treatment experience for youth from across British Columbia. Peak House operates within the harm reduction spectrum and utilizes a trauma-informed, client-centered, and social justice framework that promotes lasting change and growth for program participants.

One feature that sets Peak House apart is its collaborative, youth-driven, and community-based model of care. The program is rooted in honoring the wisdom and expertise of young persons and families, promoting social justice-informed approaches to therapy and counseling. Peak House has earned significant recognition in the addiction treatment industry including being accredited by CARF, licensed, and receiving awards like the Addiction Specialists & Allied Professionals of British Columbia (ASAP) Award of Excellence and the BC Association of Clinical Counselors Professional Care Award.

location.heading: Peak House in Vancouver, British Columbia
location.intro: Peak House is a house on a residential street in East Vancouver, and it takes youth from every part of BC, not only the Lower Mainland. Downtown Vancouver is about 15 minutes away by car, Burnaby about 10 and North Vancouver about 20 over the Ironworkers Memorial Bridge, while families coming from Surrey should allow about 40 minutes, from Victoria about 3 to 3.5 hours with the Swartz Bay to Tsawwassen ferry, and from Kelowna in the Okanagan about 4 hours by road.

faqIntro: Answers come from the original listing and Peak House's own website. Still unsure? Call the intake line, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Peak House cost?
faqs.a: Nothing. Peak House is free for youth in British Columbia because it is funded through a contract with Vancouver Coastal Health. The program is run by Pacific Youth and Family Services Society, a registered charity, so families do not pay fees or need private insurance.

faqs.q: Who can go to Peak House?
faqs.a: Peak House is for youth aged 13 to 18 who live in BC and want help with drugs, including alcohol. Young people up to 22 can be accepted case by case where licensing allows, and priority goes to youth under 19. The program is voluntary, so the young person has to want to be there, and they need a housing plan and a family member, foster parent or social worker who will support them.

faqs.q: How do I make a referral?
faqs.a: Start with the referral package on peakhouse.ca, usually filled in with an alcohol and drug counsellor or another professional who knows the young person. Peak House passes it to Vancouver Coastal Health's Youth Central Addiction Intake Team, and a committee reviews referrals every week. Parents without a counsellor can call intake at 604-253-6319, and urgent, high-risk cases can often be moved up.

faqs.q: What is the minimum and maximum stay duration?
faqs.a: The Peak House program lasts ten weeks; there is no minimum stay.

No. Peak House does not offer detox, and it asks youth to be free of all drugs and alcohol for at least seven days before they arrive. Its advice is to plan a safe cut-down with your A&D counsellor and talk about whether a detox stay is needed first.

Youth keep going to school while they live at Peak House. A full-time resource teacher from the Vancouver School Board teaches four mornings a week for two hours, and youth can earn credits such as PE, Art and Career Life Education. In summer, school time becomes a life skills program with workshops and outings.

faqs.q: How are parents and families involved?
faqs.a: Families are part of the program. The weekly schedule includes a family night, the last three weeks focus on planning the return home with family and professionals, and aftercare sessions can be family sessions. For the first month, phone calls are limited to family, caregivers and professional supports.

faqs.q: Can residents use their mobile phones?
faqs.a: Not during treatment. Peak House asks youth not to bring any device that can go online, text or take photos, so they can unplug and focus on getting well. For the first 30 days contact is usually limited to family, caregivers and professionals, and supportive friends can be added later. An MP3 player with no messaging or internet is allowed.

faqs.q: What happens after the program ends?
faqs.a: Youth are encouraged to come back for four aftercare therapy sessions, on their own or with family, and staff are available by phone. A staff-led group meets monthly for former residents, and graduates are invited back to speak with current residents.

faqs.q: Where is Peak House and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Peak House is in East Vancouver, in a house on a residential street that does not look like a hospital. It is about 15 minutes from downtown Vancouver by car and about 10 minutes from Burnaby. Youth come from all over BC, including Vancouver Island, the Okanagan and Northern BC, and the intake coordinator sets up the arrival once a referral is accepted.
No. Peak House says no single model works for everyone, but residents go to two NA or AA meetings a week so they can see whether that kind of support helps them.

faqs.q: What makes Peak House different from other facilities?
faqs.a: Peak House is a home-like facility that caters to the individual needs of teens struggling with addiction. The therapeutic approach, the recreational activities, and the skilled professionals make it unique.
The staff at Peak House are trained, experienced professionals in counseling and substance abuse.
